newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jewellers place hopes on Christmas sales.
newsitem.headline: German jewellers place hopes on Christmas sales.

text.p: Business ahead of the Christmas season has lifted the German jewellery sector after slow sales earlier in the year, industry body VDSI said on Tuesday.

"Trade orders started to pick up in August," said Alfred Schneider, general secretary of the VDSI federation of jewellery makers from the town of Pforzheim, where most fabricators and wholesale traders are based.
"It's the silver lining in a tough and sluggish year and we hope it will continue right through to the end of 1996."
Two thirds of annual jewellery sales to retailers are made in the months of November and December.
The industry in 1995 had combined sales of 2.10 billion marks, down from 2.35 billion in 1994 and 2.40 billion in 1993.
Schneider declined to give an estimate for 1996 but said sales losses earlier in the year may be offset by the improved seasonal activity.
The industry has been suffering from lower spending on luxury items in the domestic market and currency disadvantages in export markets.
